P1: C1: Continuous values are discretised (information-losing) before permutation | C2: Besides the value permutation, continuous values are discretized into ten bins, an information-losing step the base List Template does not apply.; P2: C1: Columns and names unchanged | C2: Column names and order are unchanged, and one fixed permutation per column is applied to all rows.; P3: C1: Same list length | C2: Same template and same columns.; P4: C1: Rule interpretation: the List Template, field order, task prompt and model input pathway are unchanged; only value strings differ. A consistent permutation of continuous values requires a finite value vocabulary, so binning is the vehicle of the tested manipulation rather than a change to the surrounding representation. The information loss it causes is already coded under P1 (No, agreed); coding it again under P4 would double-count. | C2: Rule interpretation first. The frozen rules score the information loss from discretizing values under P1; discretization is the rule’s own P1 example, and P1 = No is already agreed. P4 scores template, serialization, ordering or encoder changes outside the tested component. Sec. 3.2 explicitly keeps the List Template (names, column order, serialization), and in this comparison the values themselves are the tested component ("column-value meanings and representations"). The paper does not say how binned values are rendered, and even a bin-style rendering would fall inside the tested value component. P1: C1: The BRCA gene table is unchanged, but each row also carries a drug vector derived from a non-feature KG node; the paper does not say how this input was produced when non-feature nodes were removed, so preservation of that predictive input is not established. | C2: Each row also takes the drug as a ComplEx embedding of the KG drug node. Per README rule, retain Unclear. | C2: The arm is labeled only as excluding edge information. Sec. 3.1 defines the input fields by construction (one leaf per non-missing cell), and the arm’s stated scope is edge (column-name) information; neither touches the cells. Whether the edge channel was dropped, zeroed or replaced concerns the tested component itself. The tested manipulation acts on edge content, so width is established by §3.1. The undescribed edge handling remains a P4 matter. P1: C1: Ordinal encoding is a bijective (lossless) relabelling of categories; other cells untouched | C2: Only categorical/string columns are re-encoded, and ordinal codes map each category one-to-one, so the underlying values are kept.; P2: C1: One encoded column per original column | C2: Each categorical/string column becomes one code column, and column names are ablated only in the separate column-semantics rows.; P3: C1: Ordinal encoding keeps column count | C2: One ordinal value per cell leaves the number of columns unchanged.; P4: C1: Semantic text encoder replaced by a conventional encoder (encoder swap = P4 fail under the frozen rule) | C2: The text-embedding encoder for cells is replaced by ordinal encoding, a change of encoding mechanism.; P5: C1: How the ordinal codes enter the model (numeric pathway vs. text pathway vs. an added layer) is not described. | C2: The paper does not describe how the ordinal-code outputs are fed to the model. "Using the base model with one-dimensional embedding" names each block’s reference configuration: the Top block, "using the base model with binning", contains model-size ablations, so the phrase does not establish that an ablation arm keeps the base architecture.; P6: C1: Not stated whether encoder variants reuse the same checkpoint/inference protocol or were re-trained | C2: The paper does not state whether the model was retrained for this arm or the same checkpoint was evaluated, so symmetric training cannot be confirmed.

P1: C1: Hash of n-grams; losslessness for category identity not established in the paper | C2: Other columns are untouched, but MinHash is a compressive encoding of unreported dimension, so lossless preservation of the string values cannot be confirmed.; P2: A: Unclear. In ConTextTab, feature identity is carried by the header embedding summed into each cell (Sec. 3.1). MinHashEncoder emits several components per column. Whether they enter as one cell, which keeps the header mechanism, or as several new columns with undescribed headers is not reported. That is the same unreported integration detail that leaves the agreed C08-B P3 Unclear. Per-feature replacement shows that no features merge, but it does not show how identity is kept.
